name: Martin Luther King Jr. National Historical Park
unique: The block where King was born and preached, with his boyhood home, Ebenezer Baptist Church, the fire station and the tomb, all walkable and free.
buzz: The birthplace tour needs a timed ticket and sells out, so book first. The church service on Sunday is open to visitors and is the part people remember.

name: Center for Puppetry Arts
unique: A puppetry museum with Jim Henson's original Muppets, a global collection of marionettes and a working theater that stages shows for kids and adults.
buzz: The Henson gallery is the reason adults come without kids. The puppet shows cost extra and are worth it, especially the adult nights.

name: Oakland Cemetery
unique: Atlanta's oldest cemetery, with Victorian monuments, the graves of Gone with the Wind author Margaret Mitchell and golf great Bobby Jones, and a view of the skyline over the trees.
buzz: The guided tour is worth the small fee and the self guided map is free. Go in the morning for light and quiet.

name: Fox Theatre
unique: A 1929 movie palace built as a Shriners temple, with a Moorish courtyard ceiling of stars and clouds, now a touring Broadway and concert house.
buzz: The building is the attraction as much as the show. Take the tour if nothing is playing, and look up in the lobby.

name: The Clermont Lounge
unique: A dive bar in the basement of a shuttered hotel where the dancers are over forty, the drinks are cheap and the walls are covered in decades of stickers and bras.
buzz: It is not for everyone and it knows it. People either love the lack of polish or leave in ten minutes. Cash only.

name: Fernbank Museum
unique: A natural history museum with a 123 foot dinosaur hall, a giant screen theater and a forest trail with elevated walkways into old growth woods.
buzz: The dinosaurs are the kid draw and the outdoor trail is the surprise. Adults can do the museum and the forest in one visit.

name: Your DeKalb Farmers Market
unique: A 140,000 square foot indoor market run by an international staff, with produce from four continents, a bakery, a butcher and a fish counter that locals treat as a weekly ritual.
buzz: Go hungry. The cheese and olive bars are the cheap thrill, and the prepared food counter is the lunch move. Parking is a contact sport on Saturdays.

name: Arabia Mountain
unique: A bare granite monadnock with solution pits, rare plants and red pools, twenty minutes from downtown Atlanta and unlike anything else in the metro.
buzz: The loop is easy and the rock is otherworldly. Wear grippy shoes, bring water, and go early because there is no shade.

name: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park
unique: A Civil War battlefield with earthworks, cannon and a climb up the mountain for a view of the Atlanta skyline, on a green ridge inside the metro.
buzz: The trail to the top is steep but short, and the museum explains the battle clearly. Deer are common at dusk.

name: Marietta Square
unique: A 19th century courthouse square with a fountain, a theater, independent shops and a food hall, plus a farmers market that fills the streets on weekends.
buzz: The square is the social center of Cobb and the ghost tour is a local favorite. Parking is free in the deck behind the square.

name: Six Flags Over Georgia
unique: The original Six Flags park, with a wooden coaster from 1967, a hypercoaster and a water park next door, forty minutes from downtown.
buzz: Go on a weekday and buy the flash pass if you care about coasters. The food is what it is, and the parking lot is enormous.

name: Southern Museum of Civil War and Locomotive History
unique: The home of the General locomotive, stolen by Union spies in the Great Locomotive Chase of 1862, with the engine, the rail car and the spy story in one room.
buzz: The locomotive is real and the story is better than the movie. Kids love the model train layout.

name: Buford Highway
unique: A seven mile corridor of immigrant restaurants, bakeries and groceries, from Sichuan and Korean barbecue to Salvadoran pupusas and Vietnamese pho, with signs in a dozen scripts.
buzz: Pick three stops and share plates. The strip malls hide the best food in the city, and lunch is cheaper than dinner.

name: Southeastern Railway Museum
unique: A rail yard museum with locomotives, cabooses and passenger cars you can climb through, plus short train rides on weekends.
buzz: The train ride is short but the kids do not care. Volunteers are enthusiasts and will explain every engine.

name: Aurora Theatre
unique: A professional theater in a converted courthouse square building, with a mainstage season of musicals and plays and a second space for comedians and local acts.
buzz: Quality is high for a suburban company and the seats are close. The holiday show sells out early.

name: Atlanta State Farmers Market
unique: A 150 acre farmers market with sheds of peaches, greens and tomatoes sold by the growers, plus a garden center and a meat market.
buzz: Go early in summer for peaches and boiled peanuts. It is a working market, not a boutique, which is the appeal.

name: Reynolds Nature Preserve
unique: A 146 acre preserve with a lake, boardwalks, a native plant garden and a small nature center, hidden behind the commercial strip south of the airport.
buzz: Flat, shady and free, with turtles and herons on the lake. Good for small kids and a quiet hour.

name: National Archives at Atlanta
unique: The federal archives for the Southeast, with original records, photographs and exhibits, and a research room where anyone can pull files.
buzz: Not a museum in the usual sense, but the exhibits are free and the staff help family researchers. Bring ID for the research room.
